name: a shallow rain puddle lying on the ground, reflecting a pale sky band, with a soft damp earth halo and only a faint low bank shadow along its far edge
label: wasteland_ruins/puddle

surfaces.part: damp earth ground tile with small pebbles and debris

answer.evidence: The image is a full 64x48 opaque ground tile of mottled brown earth. Two teal water ellipses lie in it, one at about rows 20-28 and one at about rows 36-44. Each has a pale blue sky-reflection band and a darker navy bank shadow along its top (far) edge. Their width profiles widen and then narrow again, so they read as flat ellipses seen from above. There is no vertical front face, no eave and no side face, so the object is a flat decal lying on the ground. That matches the 'flat' kind and the top_down_slab reading. The small pale and red-brown specks near x=45-51, rows 37-44, are pebble or debris details.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts are acceptable: 4 visible tones per tile against 3 for the grass reference, 0% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the edges are tinted rather than near-black. By eye the piece is still shallow. The whole patch uses only 14 colours, against 80 for the grass reference. The earth is a brown base with sparse darker and lighter speckles, about 3 steps, and there is no visible damp halo ramp around the puddles. The puddles are small blue blobs with only 2-3 tones. They have no clear pale sky band, no highlight and no bank-shadow step. A stray reddish speckle sits near the lower puddle. Next to the grass and paving references, which have layered clumps and per-stone shading, this reads as simpler and flatter than Beodeul's 5-6 steps per material. The puddle subject is also under-developed.
